newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA FIGHTS FOOT-AND-MOUTH DISEASE OUTBREAK.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA FIGHTS FOOT-AND-MOUTH DISEASE OUTBREAK.

text.p: The Bulgarian Veterinary Service suspended livestock exports and trade in a bid to contain an foot-and-mouth disease outbreak in the southeastern village of Malko Sharkovo, the official news agency BTA said on Monday.

"Laboratory reports confirmed contamination by foot-and- mouth disease among cloven-hoofed livestock in the village of Malko Sharkovo near the town of Yambol," said BTA quoting the Veterinary Service.
The Service has placed contaminated animals under special care and "measures for localisation and liquidation of the foot-and-mouth outbreak are being taken", said BTA.
Veterinary Service officials were not immediately available for comment.

Precautions include a temporary ban on livestock traffic and hunting in the Yambol and Haskovo region near the border with Turkey. Transport is diverted from the vicinity of the village and all skin storage houses are temporarily closed.
Bulgaria last had an outbreak of the disease in 1993 and no foot-mouth-disease cases were reported since then.

Earlier in the year Bulgaria banned the imports of meat and dairy products from Greece, Turkey, rump Yugoslavia and Macedonia and withdrew its herds from the border areas, as part of precautionary measures to forestall the spread of the disease.
"It is the same virus which is widely spread among herds in neighbouring countries," said the statement. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
